title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Let X be a topological space, Y a closed subspace, and τ a germ of 'conical neighbourhood structure' of Y in X. Equivalently, Grothendieck says, X can be given by 'déploiement' (unfolding) data (X̃, Ẋ, 𝓔, Y, f):
- X̃ = X̃* is a space with a closed subspace Ẋ.
- 𝓔 is a germ of cylindrical neighbourhoods (a collar Ẋ×[0,ε)) of Ẋ in X̃.
- f: Ẋ → Y is continuous.
Then X = X̃ ⊔_Ẋ Y. Near Y, X is the open mapping cylinder of f. The cone lines are the collar lines, and the homotheties λ∈[0,1] squeeze the collar coordinate. In modern terms: a conical (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhood of Y is the same thing as a 'blow-up' or 'unzipping' X̃ of X along Y, whose new boundary Ẋ (the link bundle) maps to Y.

The page begins by finishing a remark: for a closed subset X' compatible with the conical germ, the germ of X̃'_1 = closure(X'∩X*) along Ẋ is determined by Ẋ'_1 = X̃'_1 ∩ Ẋ.

Corollary. Closed subsets X' ⊂ X compatible with the conical germ (that is, conical near Y: unions of cone rays together with points of Y) correspond bijectively to pairs (X̃' ⊂ X̃, Y' ⊂ Y) of closed subsets such that:
(a) X̃' is compatible with the cylindrical germ, i.e. X̃'∩E = Ẋ'×I near Ẋ.
(b) f maps Ẋ' := X̃'∩Ẋ into Y'.
The correspondence is X' = Im(X̃' → X) ∪ Y', where the image part is X' minus Y' and Y' = Y∩X'. Moreover X' is 'strictly conical' iff Y' = f(Ẋ'), i.e. X' has no isolated extra points of Y that are not limits of rays.

Second part: compatibility of a collar with the conical structure. Let X_0 ⊂ X be a 'bordante' (boundary-like) part, with a germ of cylindrical structure 𝓔 (a collar E ≅ X_0×I). 𝓔 is called compatible with the conical germ 𝒯 of X around Y (margin: better say 'transversal') if there exist representatives E ≅ X_0×I and T (with conical structure) such that T∩E, Ṫ∩E and Y∩E are cylindrical parts:
- T∩E ≅ T_0×I
- Ṫ∩E ≅ Ṫ_0×I
- Y∩E ≅ Y_0×I
with T_0 = X_0∩T and Y_0 = X_0∩Y. These are therefore stable under the E-homotheties.
The next page adds the symmetric condition (E∩T, Ė∩T and X_0∩T are conical in T) and commutation of the two homothety actions, so that λ_T on T∩E ≅ T_0×I is λ_{T_0}×id_I. In short, the conical structure near the boundary is the product with I of a conical structure of T_0 around Y_0.

Purpose. This is the inductive machinery for describing stratified spaces by unfolding them stratum by stratum into spaces with boundary/corners. It requires:
- a calculus of conical subspaces, to handle closed unions of strata;
- compatibility of collars ('bordante' parts) with conical structures, so that after unfolding the deepest stratum the remaining structure is still conical along the new boundary pieces.
errors: No mathematical error. Small imprecision: the bijection needs X̃' to be the closure of X'∩X* (the X̃'_1 of the previous page). Otherwise X̃' could contain spurious points of Ẋ; the condition 'compatible with the cylindrical germ' only fixes this near Ẋ, which is enough.
On this page the cylindrical identification Ṫ∩E ≅ T_0×I (written in the image) should read Ṫ∩E ≅ Ṫ_0×I. Grothendieck corrects this himself on the next page.

ideas.what: Equivalence between a conical neighbourhood germ of a closed Y in X and the unfolded data (collared space X̃ with boundary Ẋ, map f: Ẋ→Y), with X = X̃ ⊔_Ẋ Y
ideas.modern_name: mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods / blow-up ('unzipping', 'déplissage') of a stratified space along a stratum; link bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1969–70); Siebenmann (1972); Quinn (1988); Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi 'déplissage' (1990s); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping' (2017)
ideas.where_published: Sketched informally in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 on tame topology and the 'dévissage' of stratified structures; no detailed account

ideas.what: Closed conical subspaces of X correspond to pairs (cylindrically compatible X̃', Y') with f(Ẋ') ⊂ Y'; X' is strictly conical iff Y' = f(Ẋ')
ideas.modern_name: description of closed (strict) conical subspaces / substratifications in terms of the unfolding

ideas.what: Transversality of a collar of a boundary-like part X_0 with a conical structure around Y: products T_0×I etc., and commuting homothety actions
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of collars with control data / conical structures; stratified spaces with corners (product structure near the boundary)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather control data with boundary; Verona; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (conically smooth spaces with corners)

missed.claim: This is an explicit categorical formulation of the 'unzipping' of a stratified space along a closed stratum. The equivalence is between the category of (X, Y, conical germ) and the category of (collared X̃, Ẋ, map Ẋ→Y). Commuting collar and cone homotheties are used as the transversality condition needed to iterate. This is essentially the device later developed by Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzip, links, corners) and by Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (déplissage). The bare idea is in Esquisse §5; the formal treatment here is not, though it is largely standard topology.
missed.quote: On dit que 𝓔 est compatible avec le germe de structure cônique 𝒯 de X autour de Y ... (marge) au lieu de 'compatible', dire plutôt 'transversal'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck in 1981–82 was building, in categorical form, the unfolding equivalence now central to the AFT approach to stratified spaces and factorization homology. It is of historical rather than technical value.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially routine point-set development of the unfolding/mapping-cylinder description of conical neighbourhoods and of collar–cone transversality. The ideas are known (Mather, Siebenmann, Quinn, AFT) and the programme is announced in Esquisse. The value is historical anticipation, not a new result.

The underbrace under Im(X̃'→X) reads X' \ (Y∩X'), with 'Y'' written under Y∩X', meaning Y' = Y∩X'.
Bottom right: 'Y_0 = Ẋ_0 ∩ Y' should read Y_0 = X_0 ∩ Y, consistent with the next page.
In the line 'Ṫ∩E ≃ T_0×I', Grothendieck intends Ṫ_0×I, as corrected on the next page; also 'Ė' is written above the inclusion X_0 ⊂ ... ≃ X_0×I.
